answer: First the agent commits 64 GB of RAM and the verifier issues a cedar probe of one million random reads against it, each with a 90 ns access budget only a dedicated memory bus can meet. Next the verifier checks the timing signatures and flags any read slower than 120 ns as shared hardware. One honest agent passes on a 400 dollar machine, while ten fakes must each rent identical 64 GB rigs, ten times the cost, and still fail the ridge timing test together. Failed probes slash a 500 POA bond and freeze the basalt identity from grading for the epoch.
